introduction_markdown:
Multiple choice question paper, 0515 Chemistry 1, June 2019 (Cameroon GCE Board, Ordinary Level). One and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer. Calculators are allowed.

**Useful data.** Relative atomic masses: H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cl = 35.5, N = 14.0, Na = 23.0, Cu = 64.0, Zn = 65.0. 1 Faraday = 96000 coulombs. Molar volume of any gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$. Avogadro number = $6.02\times 10^{23}$. Specific heat capacity of water = $4.2\ \mathrm{J\ g^{-1}\ ^\circ C^{-1}}$.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.

Question 36 : le blanc de AgCl est-il une « couleur » ? Seconde proposition prise comme vraie (précipités blanc, crème, jaune), clé retenue A ; si le jury considère « blanc » comme non coloré, la clé serait C.

Question 47 : le schéma (capsule sur bain de vapeur) correspond à l'évaporation à sec ; la cristallisation (A) reste une lecture possible. Clé retenue C. La question 48 (NaCl et H2O) vaut D dans les deux lectures.

Question 4 : le produit solide CaO n'est pas proposé ; l'option B (NO2 et O2) est la seule dont les deux produits sont corrects.

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose a metal commonly used as overhead electric cables.
questions.corrige_markdown: Overhead cables must conduct well, be light enough to hang between pylons and resist corrosion. Aluminium is a good conductor, has a low density and is protected by a thin oxide layer, so it is used (often with a steel core for strength). Copper conducts better but is much denser and dearer; zinc and iron are poor choices. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a method that can be used to separate a mixture of water and petrol.
questions.corrige_markdown: Water and petrol are immiscible liquids of different densities: they form two layers, and petrol floats on water. A separating funnel lets the lower (water) layer run off. Evaporation and sublimation do not apply, and simple distillation is used for miscible liquids. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the atomic number of an atom with electronic configuration 2,8,8,2.
questions.corrige_markdown: In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the atomic number. $2+8+8+2=20$, so the atomic number is $20$ (calcium). Do not confuse the number of shells (4) or the outer electrons (2) with the atomic number. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate will produce;
questions.corrige_markdown: Nitrates of metals in the middle of the reactivity series, such as calcium, decompose into the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen: $2\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CaO} + 4\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$ (balanced: 2 Ca, 4 N, 12 O on each side). Of the pairs offered, only $\mathrm{NO_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ are products (together with CaO). The nitrite and $\mathrm{N_2O}$ options are not products for calcium (the nitrite is what sodium and potassium nitrates give). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transition metal used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia is
questions.corrige_markdown: In the Haber process, $\mathrm{N_2} + 3\mathrm{H_2} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_3}$, finely divided iron is the catalyst. Vanadium(V) oxide is used in the contact process (sulphuric acid) and platinum in the oxidation of ammonia (nitric acid). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The element X exists naturally as two isotopes, $^{80}\mathrm{X}$ and $^{82}\mathrm{X}$ in the ratio 1 : 1. The relative atomic mass of X will be
questions.corrige_markdown: The relative atomic mass is the weighted average of the isotopic masses. With a 1 : 1 ratio: $\frac{80\times 1 + 82\times 1}{2} = \frac{162}{2} = 81$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 7 - 9 concern the following table.*

| Element | M | N | O | P | Q |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proton | 12 | 16 | 17 | 18 | 20 |
| Electron | 12 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 20 |

M, N, O, P and Q are not the usual symbols of the elements. Each element can be selected once, more than once or not at all. Select from the table:

7. An element that will not react easily with other elements.
questions.corrige_markdown: An element is unreactive when its outer shell is full. P has $18$ protons and $18$ electrons, so its configuration is $2,8,8$: a full outer shell (argon, a noble gas). M ($2,8,2$) and Q ($2,8,8,2$) have two outer electrons and lose them readily; O ($2,8,7$) needs one electron. N (16 protons) is $2,8,6$ and needs two. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 7 - 9 concern the following table.*

| Element | M | N | O | P | Q |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proton | 12 | 16 | 17 | 18 | 20 |
| Electron | 12 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 20 |

M, N, O, P and Q are not the usual symbols of the elements. Each element can be selected once, more than once or not at all. Select from the table:

8. Elements that belong to the same group of the Period Table
questions.corrige_markdown: Elements of one group have the same number of outer-shell electrons. M ($12$ electrons: $2,8,2$) and Q ($20$ electrons: $2,8,8,2$) both have $2$ outer electrons, so both are in Group II (magnesium and calcium). N ($2,8,6$) and O ($2,8,7$) have different outer electrons, and M and N differ as well. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 7 - 9 concern the following table.*

| Element | M | N | O | P | Q |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proton | 12 | 16 | 17 | 18 | 20 |
| Electron | 12 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 20 |

M, N, O, P and Q are not the usual symbols of the elements. Each element can be selected once, more than once or not at all. Select from the table:

9. Determine the formula of the compound formed between M and N
questions.corrige_markdown: M ($2,8,2$) loses $2$ electrons to form $\mathrm{M^{2+}}$. N ($16$ protons, configuration $2,8,6$) gains $2$ electrons to form $\mathrm{N^{2-}}$. One ion of each balances the charges: $\mathrm{M^{2+}} + \mathrm{N^{2-}} \rightarrow \mathrm{MN}$ (like magnesium sulphide, MgS). The formula is $\mathrm{MN}$; $\mathrm{M_2N_2}$ is not the simplest ratio. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Give the formula of the fifth member of the homologous series with general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$
questions.corrige_markdown: The members of the series are $n=1,2,3,4,5$: methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane. The fifth member has $n=5$: $\mathrm{C_5H_{2\times5+2}} = \mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$. $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}$ belongs to the alkene series and $\mathrm{C_5H_8}$ to the alkynes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Name two air pollutants which are responsible for acid rain.
questions.corrige_markdown: Acid rain is caused by the acidic gases sulphur dioxide ($\mathrm{SO_2}$) and the oxides of nitrogen ($\mathrm{NO_2}$), which dissolve in rain water to give sulphurous/sulphuric acid and nitric acid. $\mathrm{N_2}$ is harmless and not a pollutant, and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ only gives a very weak acid (carbonic acid) and is a greenhouse gas. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following substances will burn with a smoky and luminous flame?
questions.corrige_markdown: A smoky, luminous (yellow) flame is the sign of incomplete combustion of a fuel that is rich in carbon: soot (unburnt carbon) glows in the flame. Ethene is unsaturated ($\mathrm{C_2H_4}$, about 86% carbon by mass), richer in carbon than propane (about 82%) or butane (about 83%), so it burns with a smoky luminous flame. Hydrogen burns with a pale, almost invisible flame and no soot. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the amount of substance in moles in $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{HCl(aq)}$.
questions.corrige_markdown: Amount $=$ concentration $\times$ volume in $\mathrm{dm^3}$. $250\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 0.250\ \mathrm{dm^3}$, so $n = 0.1\times 0.250 = 0.025$ mol. The trap is to forget to convert $\mathrm{cm^3}$ to $\mathrm{dm^3}$ (which gives $25$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When excess carbon dioxide is passed through lime water, the milky colour disappears due to the formation of
questions.corrige_markdown: Lime water, $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$, first turns milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms: $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaCO_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}$. With excess $\mathrm{CO_2}$ the precipitate reacts further and dissolves as soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate: $\mathrm{CaCO_3} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ca(HCO_3)_2}$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the colour imparted to a Bunsen flame by a copper (II) salt?
questions.corrige_markdown: Flame tests: copper(II) salts give a bluish-green flame. Sodium gives golden yellow, and calcium gives brick red; apple green is the colour of barium salts. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The apparatus used in preparing a standard solution is a
questions.corrige_markdown: A standard solution has an accurately known concentration. The weighed solute is dissolved and made up to the mark in a volumetric flask, which holds one exact volume. A burette and a pipette deliver measured volumes of liquid, and a measuring cylinder is not accurate enough. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: During an oxidation reaction, an oxidizing agent
questions.corrige_markdown: An oxidizing agent brings about the oxidation of another substance and is itself reduced. Reduction is loss of oxygen (or gain of electrons), so the oxidizing agent loses oxygen, for example $\mathrm{CuO}$ in $\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{H_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{H_2O}$. Gaining oxygen, losing hydrogen and losing electrons describe the substance that is oxidized (the reducing agent). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the quantity of electricity in coulombs if a current of $0.5\ \mathrm{A}$ is passed through an electrolyte for $15$ minutes.
questions.corrige_markdown: Quantity of electricity $Q = I\times t$ with $t$ in seconds. $t = 15\times 60 = 900$ s, so $Q = 0.5\times 900 = 450$ C. Using $15$ instead of $900$ gives $7.5$ (option C), which is the trap. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of replaceable hydrogen atoms in a molecule of an acid is called its
questions.corrige_markdown: The basicity of an acid is the number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule that can be replaced by a metal (or ionize as $\mathrm{H^+}$). For example, $\mathrm{HCl}$ has basicity 1 and $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ has basicity 2. Acidity and alkalinity are not terms for this, and pH measures hydrogen ion concentration. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The substance left in the glass tube when excess dry hydrogen is passed over heated copper (II) oxide is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydrogen reduces the black copper(II) oxide: $\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{H_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{H_2O}$. The water leaves as steam, and because hydrogen is in excess the reduction is complete, so the pink-brown metallic copper is what remains. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The function of limestone in the extraction of iron is to remove
questions.corrige_markdown: In the blast furnace limestone decomposes ($\mathrm{CaCO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO_2}$) and the calcium oxide combines with silica (sand, an earthy impurity) to form molten slag: $\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO_3}$, which floats on the iron and is tapped off. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Instructions: each question is followed by four responses numbered 1 - 4. One or more of these responses is (are) correct. Decide which response(s) is (are) correct, then choose:* A) If only 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B) If only 1 and 3 are correct; C) If only 2 and 4 are correct; D) If only 4 is correct.

22. The factors that influence the preferential discharge of ions during electrolysis are

1 Position of ion on the electrochemical series.

2 Nature of the electrode.

3 Concentration of the ion.

4 The charge on the ion.
questions.corrige_markdown: Three factors decide which ion is discharged: the position of the ion in the electrochemical series (statement 1), the nature of the electrode, since an active electrode such as copper can itself dissolve (statement 2), and the concentration of the ion (statement 3). The charge on the ion is not a factor (statement 4 is wrong): it only fixes how many electrons are needed. So 1, 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Instructions: each question is followed by four responses numbered 1 - 4. One or more of these responses is (are) correct. Decide which response(s) is (are) correct, then choose:* A) If only 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B) If only 1 and 3 are correct; C) If only 2 and 4 are correct; D) If only 4 is correct.

23. A catalyst is a substance which

1 Increases the temperature of a reaction

2 Increases the rate of a chemical reaction

3 Increases the yield of a chemical reaction

4 Remains chemically unchanged at the end of a reaction
questions.corrige_markdown: A catalyst speeds up a reaction (2 is true) and is unchanged chemically at the end (4 is true). It does not raise the temperature (1 is false) and it does not change the position of equilibrium, so the yield is not increased (3 is false); it only helps equilibrium to be reached faster. So 2 and 4 are correct. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The components of crude oil can be separated by
questions.corrige_markdown: Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons with different boiling points. They are separated into fractions (petrol, kerosene, diesel...) in a fractionating column by fractional distillation. Cracking and reforming change the molecules chemically, and simple distillation is not enough for a mixture of many close boiling points. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The empirical formula of an organic compound is CH. If the relative molecular mass of the compound is $78$, then the molecular formula is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The empirical formula mass of $\mathrm{CH}$ is $12 + 1 = 13$. The number of units is $\frac{78}{13} = 6$, so the molecular formula is $(\mathrm{CH})_6 = \mathrm{C_6H_6}$ (benzene). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Carbon dioxide is prepared in the laboratory by the action of dilute hydrochloric acid on marble chips. Dilute sulphuric acid is not suitable for this process because;
questions.corrige_markdown: Marble is calcium carbonate. With dilute sulphuric acid the reaction $\mathrm{CaCO_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaSO_4} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}$ starts but calcium sulphate is only sparingly soluble, so it coats the marble chips and stops the acid reaching them. The reaction then stops. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: An insoluble coat of calcium sulphate will be formed causing the reaction to stop.
The reaction will be too fast.
The reaction will be too slow.
Marble chips do not react with dilute sulphuric acid.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a carbonate that will NOT decompose when strongly heated in an open crucible.
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbonates of the most reactive metals (potassium and sodium) are stable to heat. $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$, $\mathrm{CuCO_3}$ and $\mathrm{MgCO_3}$ decompose to the oxide and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (for example $\mathrm{CuCO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{CO_2}$), whereas $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ does not decompose in an ordinary heating. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 28 - 30 concern the following substances:* A) Ammonia gas, B) Lemon juice, C) Water, D) Ethanol. Each letter can be used once, more than once or not at all. Select from A to D a substance

28. Which produces steamy fumes with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$.

*Options as printed:* A) Ammonia gas   B) Lemon juice   C) Water   D) Ethanol
questions.corrige_markdown:
Phosphorus pentachloride is the test for the hydroxyl (-OH) group: it reacts with an alcohol such as ethanol giving steamy (misty) fumes of hydrogen chloride: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + \mathrm{PCl_5} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_5Cl} + \mathrm{POCl_3} + \mathrm{HCl}$. Ethanol is the intended answer. Note that water (and lemon juice, which is mostly water) also reacts with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ giving $\mathrm{HCl}$ fumes, so the item is not perfectly discriminating; the standard textbook use of $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ is as the test for alcohols. **Most likely expected answer: D (Ethanol).**

This question is left open for self-assessment: its answer key is debatable (see the remark above), so it is not auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 28 - 30 concern the following substances:* A) Ammonia gas, B) Lemon juice, C) Water, D) Ethanol. Each letter can be used once, more than once or not at all. Select from A to D a substance

29. That will turn moist red litmus paper blue.
questions.corrige_markdown: A substance turns moist red litmus blue only if it is alkaline. Ammonia gas dissolves in the moisture on the paper to give hydroxide ions: $\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH_4^+} + \mathrm{OH^-}$. Lemon juice is acidic, and water and ethanol are neutral. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 28 - 30 concern the following substances:* A) Ammonia gas, B) Lemon juice, C) Water, D) Ethanol. Each letter can be used once, more than once or not at all. Select from A to D a substance

30. That will turn blue litmus paper red.
questions.corrige_markdown: Only an acid turns blue litmus red. Lemon juice contains citric acid. Ammonia is alkaline, and water and ethanol are neutral. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the percentage by mass of nitrogen in $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$. (RMM of $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3} = 80$)
questions.corrige_markdown: $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$ contains $2$ nitrogen atoms: $2\times 14 = 28$. Percentage $= \frac{28}{80}\times 100 = 35\%$. The trap is to count only one nitrogen atom ($17.5\%$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these halogens is the most reactive?
questions.corrige_markdown: Reactivity of the halogens decreases down Group VII because the incoming electron is added to a shell farther from the nucleus and attracted less. Fluorine, at the top of the group, is the most reactive of the four. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following occurs during the electrolysis of aqueous copper (II) sulphate using copper electrodes?
questions.corrige_markdown: With copper electrodes the anode is active: $\mathrm{Cu} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2e^-$, so the anode dissolves and gets smaller. At the cathode $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, so copper is deposited and the cathode increases in size. Copper ions removed at the cathode are replaced at the anode, so the blue colour does not fade, and no oxygen is discharged. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The colour of the solution fades
Oxygen is discharged at the anode

questions.enonce_markdown: The compound most likely to be present in a bag of fertilizer is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A good fertilizer supplies the nutrients nitrogen and phosphorus (and potassium). $(\mathrm{NH_4})_3\mathrm{PO_4}$ supplies both nitrogen and phosphorus, so it is the compound most likely to be found in a fertilizer bag. $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is common salt and has no nutrient value for plants (and harms soil), and the other two supply only nitrogen (or calcium and nitrogen). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Instructions: each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by another in the right-hand column. Decide whether each of the statements is true or false, then choose:* A) If both statements are TRUE and the second statement is the CORRECT EXPLANATION of the first; B) If both statements are TRUE but the second statement is NOT the correct explanation of the first; C) If the first statement is true but the second statement is FALSE; D) If the first statement is FALSE but the second statement is TRUE.

35. **First statement:** Elements of Group VII show similar chemical properties.

**Second statement:** Group VII elements have same number of shells.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: Group VII elements (the halogens) have similar chemical properties because they all have $7$ electrons in the outer shell. The second statement is false: the number of shells increases down the group (fluorine has $2$, chlorine $3$, bromine $4$, iodine $5$); what is the same is the number of outer electrons. First true, second false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Both true, second does not explain first

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Instructions: each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by another in the right-hand column. Decide whether each of the statements is true or false, then choose:* A) If both statements are TRUE and the second statement is the CORRECT EXPLANATION of the first; B) If both statements are TRUE but the second statement is NOT the correct explanation of the first; C) If the first statement is true but the second statement is FALSE; D) If the first statement is FALSE but the second statement is TRUE.

36. **First statement:** The presence of $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, $\mathrm{Br^-}$ and $\mathrm{I^-}$ ions in solution can be tested using $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution.

**Second statement:** All three ions form coloured precipitates with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution.

*Options as printed:* A) Both true, second explains first   B) Both true, second does not explain first   C) First true, second false   D) First false, second true
questions.corrige_markdown:
With acidified silver nitrate, chloride gives a white precipitate of $\mathrm{AgCl}$, bromide a cream precipitate of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ and iodide a yellow precipitate of $\mathrm{AgI}$. The first statement is true. The second statement is taken as true: each ion gives a precipitate of a distinguishable colour (white, cream, yellow), and this is exactly what makes the test work, so the second explains the first. (A strict reader could object that white is not a colour; the intended key is taken to be A.) **Most likely expected answer: A (Both true, second explains first).**

This question is left open for self-assessment: its answer key is debatable (see the remark above), so it is not auto-marked.

37. **First statement:** Copper will displace magnesium from a solution of a magnesium salt.

**Second statement:** Copper is below magnesium in the electrochemical series.
questions.corrige_markdown: A metal displaces another from solution only if it is higher in the electrochemical (reactivity) series. Copper is below magnesium, so it cannot displace magnesium: the first statement is false and the second is true. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Both true, second does not explain first

questions.enonce_markdown: Palm wine goes sour when exposed to air for some days because;
questions.corrige_markdown: Palm wine contains ethanol produced by fermentation. In air, bacteria (acetic acid bacteria) oxidize the ethanol to ethanoic (acetic) acid, which tastes sour: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{H_2O}$. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Glucose is converted to gluconic acid
Ethanol is converted to Ethanoic acid
Palm wine is converted to palmitic acid

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the mass of zinc that will produce $16\ \mathrm{g}$ of copper according to the equation:

$\mathrm{Zn(s)} + \mathrm{CuSO_4(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnSO_4(aq)} + \mathrm{Cu(s)}$
questions.corrige_markdown: The equation is $1:1$. Moles of Cu $= \frac{16}{64} = 0.25$ mol (Cu $= 64.0$), so $0.25$ mol of Zn reacts. Mass of Zn $= 0.25\times 65 = 16.25$ g (Zn $= 65.0$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a basic oxide?
questions.corrige_markdown: Oxides of metals are basic. $\mathrm{Na_2O}$ dissolves in water to give sodium hydroxide, $\mathrm{Na_2O} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaOH}$. $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is acidic, $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ is amphoteric and CO is neutral. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the mass of $0.1$ mole of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$? (RMM of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3} = 106$)
questions.corrige_markdown: Mass $=$ moles $\times$ molar mass $= 0.1\times 106 = 10.6$ g. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Plastics pollute the environment because they are;
questions.corrige_markdown: Most plastics are made of synthetic polymers that bacteria cannot break down, so they are non-biodegradable and accumulate as waste. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The different components of universal indicator solution can best be separated by
questions.corrige_markdown: Universal indicator is a mixture of dyes that are soluble in the solvent but differ in how strongly they stick to the paper. They are separated by chromatography, each dye travelling a different distance. Distillation and filtration cannot separate dyes of similar boiling points or fully dissolved dyes. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Consider the equation

$\mathrm{NaOH(aq)} + \mathrm{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$ $\Delta H = X$ kJ

What does X represent?
questions.corrige_markdown: The reaction is between an acid and a base giving a salt and water, and $\Delta H$ is the heat change: this is the heat (enthalpy) of neutralization. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
$0.1\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{HCl}$ reacts with powdered $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ according to the equation

$2\mathrm{HCl(aq)} + \mathrm{Na_2CO_3(s)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)} + \mathrm{CO_2(g)}$.

How can the reaction be made to go faster?
questions.corrige_markdown: A higher concentration of acid means more frequent collisions, so using $0.5\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{HCl}$ speeds up the reaction. Lumps of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ (smaller surface area than the powder), adding water (dilution) and using $0.01\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{HCl}$ all slow it down. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Adding water to the reaction mixture

questions.enonce_markdown: How many particles of NaOH are contained in $0.1$ mole of NaOH?
questions.corrige_markdown: One mole contains $6.02\times 10^{23}$ particles (Avogadro number). For $0.1$ mol: $0.1\times 6.02\times 10^{23} = 6.02\times 10^{22}$ particles. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 47 and 48 are based on the diagram below.*

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

*The diagram shows an evaporating dish holding salt solution, placed over a beaker of boiling water (steam bath) on a gauze, heated from below.*

47. What method of separation is illustrated in the diagram?

*Options as printed:* A) Crystallization   B) Sublimation   C) Evaporation to dryness   D) Filtration
questions.corrige_markdown:
The salt solution in the dish is heated gently by the steam from the boiling water, so the water evaporates and leaves the dissolved solid behind: this is evaporation to dryness (a steam bath gives gentle, even heating of a solution). Filtration separates an insoluble solid, and sublimation does not involve a solution. Crystallization (option A) is the other possibility for a salt solution, but it would stop at the saturation point and then cool the solution, which the diagram does not show. **Most likely expected answer: C (Evaporation to dryness).**

This question is left open for self-assessment: its answer key is debatable (see the remark above), so it is not auto-marked.

48. An example of a mixture that can be separated by this method is
questions.corrige_markdown: The method separates a dissolved solid from its liquid solvent, so the mixture must be a salt in water: $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$. Kerosene and water are separated with a separating funnel, ethanol and water by fractional distillation, and $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ and $\mathrm{NaCl}$ (two solids) by sublimation of the ammonium chloride. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the process that involves a physical change.
questions.corrige_markdown: A physical change makes no new substance and is easily reversible. Heating candle wax melts it, and the wax solidifies again on cooling: physical change. Electrolysing dilute $\mathrm{NaCl}$, burning sodium and corrosion all form new substances (chemical changes). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Isotopes of a given element have the same
questions.corrige_markdown: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons. They have the same number of protons, so the same atomic number, but different mass numbers and slightly different physical properties. **Answer: D.**
